summary: GRAVEYARD falsification pass challenged all 12 b03 names. It does not manufacture bearishness: current primary evidence yields concrete falsifiers for TER, AUR, PWR, CEG and SMR; seven names remain explicitly under-acquired.

materialFindings.finding: Falsifier: AI-test growth can be real while economics remain fragile to a handful of specifiers/purchasers and Taiwan exposure; top-five direct customers were 44%, one direct customer 19%, Taiwan 36%. Robotics revenue also fell 15.5% in 2025.
Needs current primary evidence before testing automation-cycle sensitivity, software mix and acquisition/debt assumptions.
Needs current primary evidence before testing OEM concentration, ADAS pricing pressure and autonomy timetable credibility.
Needs current primary evidence before testing dilution, partner concentration, unit economics and fleet-scaling claims.

Falsifier is straightforward: technical commercialization may take longer or never achieve scale; 2025 loss was $816M, future capital may exceed expectations, 21M warrants remained outstanding, and dual-class governance concentrates voting power.
Needs current primary evidence before challenging data-center demand extrapolation, capacity constraints and acquisition integration.

Falsifier: backlog/infrastructure demand does not guarantee margin conversion. Fixed-price/EPC work faces schedule, supplier/subcontractor, liquidated-damage and wildfire liability risks; ten largest customers were 30% of revenue.
Needs current primary evidence before challenging backlog quality, project concentration and capacity-cycle durability.

Falsifier: nuclear fleet scarcity value depends partly on regulatory/license duration and policy economics. Current license-renewal applications support duration but are applications, not completed approvals.
Needs current primary evidence before challenging merchant-power exposure, hedging, fuel availability and data-center contract economics.
Needs current primary evidence before challenging customer concentration, financing dependence, service economics and deployment claims.

Falsifier: NRC certification is not commercial proof. Issuer itself flags lack of binding module contracts, uncertain SMR market growth, constrained supply, funding needs, customer approvals, construction risk and dilution.

contradictions: Strong secular demand can coexist with concentration and execution fragility at TER and PWR.
CEG license-extension action is evidence of asset-duration intent, not final regulatory approval.
SMR design certification is technologically meaningful but not evidence of cost-competitive deployed plants.
unknowns: Current falsification evidence remains incomplete for ROK, MBLY, SERV, ETN, POWL, VST and BE.
peerRequests: Company-underwriting/Deep Runner: acquire current primary anchors for the seven under-acquired names so Beta can falsify concrete claims rather than generic industry risks.
blockingIssues: Seven b03 companies lack sufficient current primary evidence for reproducible red-team treatment.
